title: Script Master
objective: Build a complete parametric tower: scale, twist and stack a polygon, then loft it.
learn: Everything: lists, data matching, transforms and surfaces in one workflow.

nodes.hint: Curve › Primitive. Radius plus a number of sides.
nodes.correct: Polygon draws a regular floor plate with S sides around the origin — the seed of the tower.

wrong.circle: A circle has no corners to twist — the Sides slider needs a polygon.
wrong.rectangle: Rectangle is always four-sided; the brief wants adjustable sides.
wrong.*: This slot needs a regular many-sided floor plate.

nodes.correct: Series gives one value per floor. The same list will drive scale, twist and height — one source of truth.

wrong.range: Range divides a domain; Series sets floor height directly as the step.
wrong.slider: One slider is one value; we need one per floor.
wrong.*: This slot needs one value per floor.

nodes.need: a way to reshape the values into a pinched profile
nodes.hint: Params › Input. Draw the curve you want the numbers to follow.
nodes.correct: Graph Mapper reads each value off an editable curve — here a dip in the middle, so middle floors get smaller factors: the waist of the tower.

wrong.remap: Remap rescales linearly — it can’t create a dip in the middle.
wrong.sine: Sine would oscillate with height, not form one smooth waist.
wrong.*: This slot needs a way to reshape the values into a pinched profile.

nodes.correct: Unit Z turns each floor value into an upward vector — the lift for each plate.

wrong.*: This slot needs upward vectors, one per floor.

nodes.need: a transform that resizes the floor plate by each factor
nodes.correct: Scale with one polygon and a LIST of factors produces a list of polygons — data matching does the copying. Centre C defaults to the origin, which is exactly where the polygon sits.

wrong.offset: Offset changes size by a distance, not a proportion; corners would drift.
wrong.*: This slot needs a transform that resizes the floor plate by each factor.

nodes.need: a transform that twists each plate by its angle
nodes.correct: Rotate turns each plate by its own angle (value × Twist). Rotating before moving keeps every plate spinning around the tower’s axis.

wrong.move: Move comes later — rotate first, while plates are still centred on the origin.
wrong.*: This slot needs a transform that twists each plate by its angle.

nodes.need: a transform that lifts each plate into place
nodes.correct: Move lifts plate i by vector i. Scaled, twisted and stacked — the tower is ready to skin.

wrong.extrude: Extrude would turn each plate into a prism, all starting from the ground.
wrong.*: This slot needs a transform that lifts each plate into place.

nodes.need: a component that skins one surface through all the floor plates
nodes.correct: Loft skins one continuous surface through every plate. Change any slider and the whole tower updates — you’ve built a parametric system.

wrong.boundary: Boundary Surfaces would cap each floor separately.
wrong.pipe: Pipe would make tubes along each outline.
wrong.*: This slot needs a component that skins one surface through all the floor plates.

check.prompt: Which input of Scale receives the Graph Mapper values?
check.hint: G = geometry, C = centre, F = factor.
check.correct: F is the scale factor. A list of factors = a list of scaled floor plates.

wrong.G: G is the geometry — the polygon is already there.
wrong.C: C is the centre point. Leaving it empty scales about the origin, which is what we want.

check.prompt: Which input of Move takes the Unit Z vectors?
check.correct: T is the motion vector — one per plate.

wrong.G: G already receives the rotated plates.
